target_customer: Developers building browser based, compute intensive or collaborative apps that need a dedicated backend per user session
problem: Giving each user a dedicated, short lived backend, as Figma and GitHub Codespaces do, is hard to build and operate for most teams.
business_model: Usage based infrastructure platform plus open source tools (Plane, Y-Sweet)
product_category: Session backend and realtime sync infrastructure

founders.name: Paul Butler
previous_startups: Botnet detection at an adtech startup (name not given)

founders.name: Taylor Baldwin
education: Bachelor's and master's in piano performance and pedagogy
founders.background_notes: Built WebGL data visualization apps; Modal's post also mentions New York Times R&D.

technical_complexity.rationale: Orchestrating per session containers with fast startup, routing and automatic shutdown, then building an open source orchestrator, is infrastructure engineering at a level hard for a small team.

defensibility.rationale: Core tools were open source, and larger platforms could offer comparable per session compute.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Modal acquired it in July 2025 and moved its functionality onto Modal's platform.

market_need_then: The founders pointed to Figma and Codespaces as proof the architecture works but is hard to replicate; no dated third party demand data found.

branding.domain_note: Used jamsocket.com, with the company blog on jamsocket.xyz.

identity.voice_and_tone: Technical blog; tagline The painless session backend platform

branding.brand_signature: Session backends as a named concept, from the founder's January 2022 post

brand_strength.rationale: Coined a concept (session backends) and shipped open source tools, but search returned no press or community evidence about the brand itself. The company legally operated as Drifting in Space, a different name.

outcome_analysis: Jamsocket raised a 2.5 million seed in August 2022 and built session backend infrastructure with open source Plane and Y-Sweet, later adding ForeverVM for AI code execution. Modal acquired it in July 2025, saying the platform suits AI heavy workloads, with undisclosed terms and no traction numbers. The AI shift gave the infrastructure a new audience, but the company stayed small and was absorbed.
notes: Seed figure is from the company's own post per search snippet (the fetch returned empty); trackers say 3M or 500K, treated as unreliable. Sources date the seed to 2022-08-11 while PitchBook says 2022-04. Competitor search found no dated competitor near batch, so the list is empty. The legal entity is Drifting in Space.
